message.content:
I don’t have direct access to external services (including VirusTotal) so I can’t pull the record myself.  
However, you can retrieve the CAA records yourself quite easily—here’s a quick way to do it:

---

### Option 1 – Use `curl` + VirusTotal Public API  

```bash
API_KEY="ig_key001"
DOMAIN="instagram.com"

curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/${DOMAIN}/dns_records/CaaRecord \
     --header "x-apikey: ${API_KEY}" |
jq .
```

* **What it does**  
  * Calls VT’s “DNS Records” endpoint filtered for type `CaaRecord`.  
  * Uses your supplied API key (`ig_key001`).  
  * Pipes output through `jq` for pretty‑printing.

> ⚠️ If you’re running this inside a script or CI pipeline, make sure the key stays secret!

---

### Option 2 – Pure DNS Query (no API)

If you just want the raw DNS data without involving VirusTotal, you can fetch the CAA records directly from the authoritative name servers:

```bash
dig @ns1.google-dns.net instagram.com CAA +short
```

or

```bash
host -t caa instagram.com
```

These commands will return whatever CAA records are published at the time of the lookup.

---

#### Quick sanity check

Running either method usually yields something along the lines of:

| Tag | Value | Issuer Domain |
|-----|-------|---------------|
| issue | letsencrypt.org | letsencrypt.org |

(Actual values may vary.)

---

Let me know if you'd prefer a different approach (e.g., Python script, PowerShell), or if you run into any errors while executing one of those snippets!
